To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Na(+)-dependent intracellular alkalinization is significantly greater in vascular smooth muscle cell cultures from SHR and Wistar rats than in WKY rats.
the activity of Na(+)-H(+) antiport in vascular smooth muscle is higher in SHR and normotensive Wistar rats than WKY rats.
the activity of Na(+)-H(+) antiport is increased in the vascular smooth muscle cells from the spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR), compared with the Wistar-Kyo rats (WKY).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Na(+)-dependent H+ extrusion system of vascular smooth muscle cells from spontaneously hypertensive rats and normotensive Wistar and Wistar-Kyto rats.
the Na(+)-dependent regulation of intracellular pH in vascular smooth muscle and the role that it may play in the development of hypertension.
the role of the Na(+)-(H+)-exchanger (NHE) in the development and/or maintenance of hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Na(+)-dependent pH regulatory mechanism in vascular smooth muscle of the SHR is similar to that found in the Wistar rat and is different from that found in the normotensive WKY rat.
Na(+)-H + antiport activity is not the primary cause of hypertension in the SHR.
increased activity of the Na+-H+ antiport in vascular smooth muscle of SHR and Wistar rats is not a specific feature of the hypertension in SHR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Na(+)-dependent pH regulatory system is more efficient in the SHR vascular cells than in WKR cells, but this difference cannot explain hypertension in the SHR.
the Na(+)-dependent pH regulatory system is not a primary cause of the hypertension in the SHR, but rather is a consequence of the hypertension.
SHR and WKY cells are similar in the Na(+)-dependent pH regulation, whereas SHR and Wistar cells are different.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Na(+)-dependent pH recovery in vascular smooth muscle is not the only determinant of blood pressure.
the Na(+)-dependent H+ extrusion system is higher in vascular smooth muscle of the SHR and Wistar rat than in WKY rat.
the Na(+)-dependent H+ transport activity in vascular cells is not necessarily a marker for hypertension.
